key_insight: Nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells do more than trap light: they also improve wetting, crystal quality, charge extraction, and mechanical robustness.
engineering_relevance: Texture engineering is a multi-functional design lever that can raise efficiency and device durability in perovskite photovoltaics and related optoelectronics.
method: Review of recently reported nano- and micro-texture effects in perovskite-based devices
Comparative focus on non-optical benefits: wetting, crystallinity, carrier extraction, and flexibility
Synthesizes texture-related mechanisms across solar cells, photodetectors, and LEDs
evidence_signal: The paper is a literature review that summarizes recent reports and observed improvements, rather than presenting a single new experimental dataset.
watch_item: Texture fabrication must be controlled carefully because the same structures that improve performance can also complicate film formation, stress management, or scalable manufacturing.
paper_title: More than just light management -- The multiple advantages of nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells
